text:
🪔 Mahavira Nirvana Diwas 2026 | November 8 🙏

An important spiritual observance in Jainism, commemorating the attainment of nirvana (final liberation) by Lord Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara.

📜 History & Origin

According to Jain tradition, Lord Mahavira attained nirvana at Pavapuri in present-day Bihar in 527 BCE, although historians debate the exact chronology.

His liberation marked freedom from the cycle of birth, death and rebirth.

Jain traditions associate the lighting of lamps with Mahavira's nirvana, symbolising the continuation of spiritual knowledge after his departure.

🪷 How It's Observed

🛕 Temple Prayers: Devotees visit Jain temples and offer prayers honouring Lord Mahavira.

🪔 Lighting Diyas: Lamps symbolise the light of wisdom overcoming ignorance.

🧘 Meditation & Reflection: Followers reflect on ahimsa (nonviolence), truth, compassion and self-discipline.

🤝 Charity & Kindness: Many practise generosity, helping others and caring for living beings.

📅 Jain New Year: In several Jain communities, the day following Diwali marks the beginning of a new year.

✨ Spiritual Significance

Lord Mahavira's teachings emphasise nonviolence, truth, non-attachment and respect for all living beings.

His message reminds us that lasting happiness comes not merely from material possessions but from inner peace, compassion and freedom from attachment.

🙏 May this sacred occasion inspire kindness, harmony and spiritual enlightenment.

#MahaviraNirvanaDiwas #Jainism #Ahimsa

text:
The U.S. Central Command has established a new “Iron Gate” task force of roughly 20 personnel based in Tampa, Florida. Its main role is to coordinate with other U.S. government agencies to disrupt the flow of advanced weapons, dual-use technologies, sanctioned goods, and illicit revenue across Iran’s land borders and through the Caspian Sea.
This comes after the U.S. already imposed a maritime blockade on Iran’s southern ports, which the military estimates has already prevented more than $25 billion in Iranian crude exports. The new task force is meant to tighten the remaining land and Caspian routes, making it harder for Iran to obtain weapons, production equipment, and hard currency — and therefore harder to rebuild military capabilities damaged by the conflict.
For Iran, oil revenues are already under heavy pressure. Further restrictions on the remaining trade and financial channels would likely raise the cost of imports and add more strain on both fiscal balances and foreign-exchange reserves.
On oil prices, I’m currently short, but I don’t think this is a situation to short blindly. While Democrats have outlined plans to wind down the U.S.-Iran confrontation, that process is unlikely to begin before next year at the earliest. For now, Trump still holds the initiative and continues to squeeze Iran’s room to maneuver.
From an outside perspective, these moves are not meaningless. Iran is already facing significant domestic pressures — rising inflation, higher prices, and a depreciating currency. Trump appears to be trying to force a quicker concession. At the same time, isolating Iran further may also increase the incentive for outside actors to offer it assistance.
Looking ahead, I expect Iran to step up its countermeasures. Militarily, however, its options are limited. This is different from the leverage it has held over oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz; in a more direct, localized confrontation, Iran’s odds do not look favorable. The bigger risk is that Tehran might abandon conventional rules — last month there were already reports suggesting it could consider using chemical weapons.
As for my own position, my oil trade that was up more than 35% earlier today has now given back almost all of those gains and is barely in positive territory.

text:
You want doom and gloom? Imagine a rural Florida county where nearly every homeowner is exempt from property taxes, but the sheriff still needs deputies, ambulances still have to arrive, and fire trucks still cost $1 million.

Now imagine the state backfill never materializes. Deputies disappear, fire stations close, ambulance response times grow, and roads deteriorate. Businesses leave, property values fall, and the remaining tax base shrinks.

Then a billion-dollar data center comes knocking. The same community that once rejected it over concerns about electricity, water, and quality of life suddenly sees it as the only way to keep the sheriff’s office funded.

Tallahassee offers three choices: permanent financial dependency, consolidation, or industrial development the community never wanted.

Here’s the cruelest part. For decades, Florida encouraged these communities to build schools, roads, fire stations, and public services around a property-tax system the state itself established.

We encouraged them to build their communities around that system, then dismantled it on a Tuesday.

The wealthy communities will adapt. The poorest may lose the very thing they were promised government would protect: local control.

We didn’t eliminate the cost of government. We eliminated the ability of some communities to pay for it.

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

Bridgerton Season 4 — The Regency-era drama returns later in the month (Part 1 premiering around Jan 29), with plenty of masquerade glamour and romance — the premiere events are already making waves!

Other notables include:

Kidnapped: Elizabeth Smart (true-crime docuseries)

New seasons of hits like Unlocked: A Jail Experiment, Love Is Blind: Germany, and WWE Unreal

Stand-up specials and reality shows keeping the variety flowing.

Plus, don't miss the Stranger Things 5 making-of documentary One Last Adventure, which premiered earlier this month for fans wanting a deep dive into the finale. Netflix is clearly doubling down on big stars, book adaptations, and high-energy originals to keep viewers hooked in 2026. (Grok)

Netflix is a global streaming service providing a vast library of films, TV shows, documentaries, and mobile games. As of 2026, it has approximately 325 million paid members across more than 190 countries.

Pricing & Plans: Subscription plans typically range from $7.99 to $24.99 per month.

Content Offerings: Includes "Netflix Originals" (like Stranger Things and Squid Game), licensed content, and a growing selection of live programming and video podcasts.

Device Compatibility: Streamable on smart TVs, game consoles, smartphones, tablets, and via https://t.co/YlumK0CxOt.

Features: Supports offline downloads, personalized recommendations, and a dedicated "Netflix Kids" experience with parental controls.

Recent 2026 Developments

Warner Bros. Merger News: As of January 21, 2026, Netflix has moved toward an all-cash $27.75-per-share offer to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, aiming to outbid Paramount.

Market Reaction: Despite a Q4 earnings beat, Netflix shares saw a 7% decline in some markets (e.g., Frankfurt) on January 21, 2026, due to investor concerns regarding the financial weight of the Warner Bros. acquisition.

Live Events: Upcoming live events include the world-record climber Alex Honnold's "Skyscraper Live" ascent of Taipei 101 on January 23, 2026.

(In Case You Missed It)

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Seasons & Episodes

The series has released two seasons as of January 2026:

Season 1: Premiered July 29, 2025. It chronicled the lead-up to the debut of WWE Raw on Netflix and WrestleMania 41. Notable segments included a look at John Cena's high-profile storyline turns and the return of Charlotte Flair.

Season 2: Released January 20, 2026. This five-episode season focuses on the "Road to SummerSlam 2025" and features superstars like Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Rhea Ripley, and Cody Rhodes.

It delves into real-life drama such as R-Truth's contract negotiations and Naomi's previous walkout from the company.

Season 3: Confirmed to be in development, expected to focus on John Cena's retirement tour.

Key Personalities Featured

Executives: Paul "Triple H" Levesque (Narrator), Peyton Manning (Executive Producer).

Superstars: John Cena, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, Seth Rollins, and Bianca Belair.

Merchandise

Related promotional items and apparel are available, including:

Action Figures: Mattel has released sets like the "Hall of Champions" 4-pack featuring legendary superstars seen in the series.

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Seasons & Episodes

The series has released two seasons as of January 2026:

Season 1: Premiered July 29, 2025. It chronicled the lead-up to the debut of WWE Raw on Netflix and WrestleMania 41. Notable segments included a look at John Cena's high-profile storyline turns and the return of Charlotte Flair.

Season 2: Released January 20, 2026. This five-episode season focuses on the "Road to SummerSlam 2025" and features superstars like Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Rhea Ripley, and Cody Rhodes.

It delves into real-life drama such as R-Truth's contract negotiations and Naomi's previous walkout from the company.

Season 3: Confirmed to be in development, expected to focus on John Cena's retirement tour.

Key Personalities Featured

Executives: Paul "Triple H" Levesque (Narrator), Peyton Manning (Executive Producer).

Superstars: John Cena, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, Seth Rollins, and Bianca Belair.

text:
I was barely 18. I was still trying to figure out which college I would attend, and suddenly I was being asked to figure out how to raise a child.

Eventually, I took her home to meet my mother.

My mother was polite. She welcomed her, offered her something to eat, and sat down to have a conversation with her.

But something happened during that conversation.

After my girlfriend left, my mother called me into her room.

She looked at me for a moment and said, “Son, I’m not convinced you’re the father of that child.”

I laughed because I thought she was joking.

She wasn’t.

I asked her why she would say something like that, but she didn’t elaborate. She simply told me to be careful and not make decisions that could permanently change my life without knowing what I was getting into.

I thought my mother was being unnecessarily suspicious.

I was in love, or at least I believed I was, and I didn’t want to be the kind of man who abandoned a woman because an unexpected pregnancy had interrupted his plans.

So I made a decision.

I would step up.

I started attending hospital appointments with her. I rearranged my football training around her medical appointments. I began thinking about diapers, baby clothes, hospital bills, and where we would live.

My girlfriend was also trying to figure out her future. She had just finished high school and was preparing for college.

I convinced myself that we could grow together.

I was ready to become a father at 18, even though I would be turning 19 soon.

My mother, however, never changed her position.

There was one particular family dinner I’ll never forget.

Everybody was seated around the dining table when my mother suddenly looked at me and asked, “Have you actually considered whether that child is yours?”

The entire table went quiet.

My girlfriend looked offended. I was embarrassed. I told my mother that she needed to stop bringing it up because I had already made my decision.

My mother didn’t argue.

She just continued eating.

A few months later, the baby arrived.

I was in the delivery room when my girlfriend gave birth. I held her hand through the entire process. I watched her go through the pain, and when the nurse finally announced that we had a healthy baby boy, I was overwhelmed.

I cried.

I took pictures of my son and immediately sent them to our family group chat.

I expected congratulations. I expected my mother to finally soften and welcome her grandson.

Instead, her first response was:

“Get a DNA test.”

I thought it was a joke.

But she said it again.

And again.

For the next three days, every time my mother spoke about the baby, she brought up the DNA test.

Not once did she ask about his weight, whether he was sleeping well, or how his mother was recovering.

It was always the same thing.

“Get a DNA test.”

Eventually, I couldn’t ignore it anymore.

I approached my girlfriend and told her I wanted us to do a paternity test.

She was furious.

She accused me of allowing my mother to poison my mind. She said I had humiliated her after everything she had gone through during pregnancy and childbirth.

I tried explaining that I wasn’t accusing her of anything. I just needed to know.

After several arguments, she eventually agreed.

We submitted the samples.

Then came the waiting.

Those days were some of the longest of my life.

I would check my email repeatedly. Sometimes I’d wake up in the middle of the night and remember that the result was still pending.

I was terrified of what I might find.

Not because I had any concrete reason to doubt her, but because I had spent months building an entire future around the belief that I was somebody’s father.

I had already started imagining his first day of school, teaching him football, taking him to my college games, and watching him grow up.

I had even begun thinking about how I would balance fatherhood with the football opportunities coming my way.

Me: “I thought you were happy being home with the children.”

Wife: “I love our children. That doesn't mean I stopped having dreams of my own.”

The therapist nodded.

Therapist: “Do you think your husband understands how much you've missed working?”

Wife: “I don't think he does. Sometimes I feel like he sees me as someone whose only responsibility is taking care of the house and children.”

Me: “That's not how I see you.”

Wife: “Then why do I have to explain that I want something for myself?”

Me: “Because I honestly thought we were doing fine. I work, I pay the bills, I make sure everyone has what they need. I didn't know you were this unhappy.”

Wife: “I'm not unhappy with our marriage. I'm unhappy with how much of myself I've had to put aside.”

There was a brief silence.

Therapist: “And what made you apply for the Chicago position?”

Wife: “A former colleague sent me the vacancy. I wasn't even sure I'd qualify, but I applied anyway. I wanted to see if I still had a chance.”

Me: “And you got the job?”

Wife: “Yes. They offered me almost twice what I used to earn.”

Me: “Twice?”

Wife: “Yes.”

Me: “You could have at least told me that part.”

Wife: “I wanted to. But I was scared you'd make me feel guilty for even considering it.”

Therapist: “What would you have wanted him to say when you first told him?”

Wife: “Honestly? I wanted him to be happy for me. Even if we eventually decided that moving wasn't possible, I wanted him to know how much this meant to me.”

I turned toward her.

Me: “I'm sorry. I didn't realize you'd been carrying all of this.”

Wife: “I know you work hard. I see it. But sometimes I need you to remember that I'm a person outside being your wife and the children's mother.”

Me: “That's fair.”

Therapist: “And what would make you comfortable moving forward?”

Me: “I want us to make decisions together. I don't want to wake up one morning and discover that my wife has already planned a completely different life.”

Wife: “I understand. I should have talked to you first.”

The therapist smiled.

Therapist: “That's a good place to start. You both seem to want the same thing: a marriage where neither person feels left behind.”

My wife nodded.

Wife: “There's something else I wanted to tell you.”

I looked at her...

Therapist: “So, how did you find out your wife was applying for jobs in another state?”

Me: “I found out because I came home from work and saw an offer letter on the kitchen counter. Chicago. A job I'd never heard her mention before.”

Wife: “I wasn't hiding it from him. I just didn't know how to bring it up.”

Me: “You didn't know how to tell your husband you were considering moving hundreds of miles away?”

Therapist: “Let's hear her side. Why didn't you tell him?”

Wife: “Because I knew what his reaction would be. He'd immediately start talking about the children, our house, his job, and everything that could go wrong.”

Me: “Well, those things matter. We have two children. We can't just wake up and decide to move because someone offered you a job.”

Wife: “I know that. I'm not stupid. I just wanted to do something for myself for once.”

Me: “You've never been stopped from doing anything.”

Wife: “Really? When was the last time I had the chance to focus on my career?”

I looked at her but didn't answer.

🪔 தமிழர் தீபாவளி மரபுகள் | Tamil Deepavali Traditions ✨

Deepavali in Tamil Nadu is a celebration of faith, family, heritage and the victory of good over evil.

📜 History & Origin

According to Hindu mythology, Deepavali commemorates Lord Krishna's victory over Narakasura, a powerful ruler associated with oppression and injustice.

In several traditional accounts, Satyabhama plays an important role in Narakasura's defeat.

The festival is associated with Naraka Chaturdashi, symbolising the destruction of evil and the beginning of a brighter life.

🌅 How Tamil Nadu Celebrates

🛁 Ganga Snanam: Families wake before sunrise, apply sesame oil and take a traditional oil bath, considered spiritually purifying.

👗 New Clothes: Elders bless younger family members, who wear new festive attire.

🍬 Traditional Delicacies: Adhirasam, murukku, mixture, laddu and other homemade sweets and savouries are prepared and shared.

🌿 Deepavali Marundhu (Legiyam): A traditional herbal preparation consumed in many households, especially during festive meals.

🪔 Prayers & Celebrations: Homes are decorated with kolam and lamps. Families offer prayers, visit temples, exchange greetings and enjoy festive meals together.

🎇 Firecrackers are also part of celebrations in many households, subject to local regulations.

❤️ Cultural Significance

Unlike the predominantly evening-focused Lakshmi Puja traditions of northern India, Tamil Deepavali celebrations often begin before sunrise.

Beyond the festivities, Deepavali preserves generations of family customs, bringing loved ones together through faith, food, gratitude and shared memories.

text:
*The Destruction of Narakasura: Dispelling Ignorance through Knowledge*

*Naraka Chaturdashi is the second day of the five-day festival of Diwali. On this day, Lord Sri Krishna traveled to the city of Pragjyotishapura and, using the Sudarshana Chakra, destroyed the demon Narakasura. The term 'Prag' means 'before' or 'at the beginning,' and 'Jyoti' means 'light.' Before light exists darkness, and it was within this darkness that Naraka resided. 'Naraka' can also be interpreted as a 'wicked human' (dushta narudu). While the virtuous transform darkness into light, the wicked turn light into darkness. To transform darkness into light, one requires 'Sudarshana'—which signifies 'right vision' or 'true knowledge.' Knowledge is, in essence, 'light.' The deeper meaning behind the destruction of Narakasura lies in dispelling darkness with light, replacing sorrow with joy, and eradicating ignorance through knowledge.*

*The five sensory organs (jnanendriyas), the five organs of action (karmendriyas), along with Prakriti (nature), Mahattattva (the cosmic intellect), and Ahamkara (ego)—these thirteen elements, when guided by the Buddhi (higher intellect), constitute the fourteen (chaturdasha) components represented by 'Chaturdashi.'*

*Thus, the destruction of Narakasura by Lord Krishna using the Sudarshana Chakra symbolizes the removal of ignorance, sorrow, and darkness through the power of profound joy, true wisdom, and radiant light.* Symbolizing this, on this day, the women of the household wake up during the *Brahmi Muhurtha* (the auspicious pre-dawn hours). They regard the couples in the home as manifestations of Lakshmi and Narayana, perform *mangala arati* (offering of sacred lights) for them, and assist them with an *abhyangana snanam* (a ritual ceremonial bath). This *mangala arati* is intended to ward off the 'evil eye' (*drishti dosha*) from Satyabhama and Krishna, who had just vanquished the demon Narakasura. The deeper significance of Deepavali is that the lamps lit in front of every home—marking their victory—serve as these very *mangala aratis* offered to Satyabhama and Krishna.

*┈┉┅━❀꧁Deepavali꧂❀━┅┉┈*
*Spiritual Seekers*

text:
Your SaaS demo might be starting at the wrong moment.

Most founders begin by showing their dashboard.

The features.
The integrations.
The automation.
The beautiful interface they spent months building.

But here’s something I’ve been learning.

Your customers don’t wake up thinking about software features.

They wake up thinking about the work they need to get done.

The orders they haven’t processed.

The customers they forgot to follow up with.

The reports they still need to prepare.

The repetitive tasks waiting for them every morning.

And that’s where your marketing should begin.

I’m Roktim, a solo founder from India.

While building my own SaaS products, I’ve realized that showing people what software can do isn’t always enough.

You need to help them imagine what their working day could look like after using it.

Here’s an example.

Imagine you’ve built order management software for small wholesale businesses.

Instead of starting your video with:

“Introducing our advanced order management dashboard.”

Start with something like:

“It’s Monday morning. You’re checking WhatsApp messages, updating spreadsheets, and trying to remember which customer ordered what.”

Now the business owner recognizes the situation.

Then show how your software could simplify that process.

That’s a much more meaningful demonstration.

You’re not just showing software. You’re showing the difference it could make in someone’s day.

But here’s the challenge.

Creating content like this consistently takes time.

Understanding customer problems.

Finding relevant topics.

Writing scripts.

Producing videos.

Researching SEO opportunities.

Creating articles and publishing everything.

And next week, you repeat the process.

When you’re also building software, fixing bugs, and talking to customers, it becomes exhausting.

That’s one of the reasons I built two tools, now offered together through Verthilix.

🎬 Vlozy: Short-form video marketing.

Turn customer problems and product benefits into videos.

✅ Hooks, music, captions, and descriptions.
✅ Publishing to connected social accounts.
✅ Performance reviews every 14 days.

📝 Blogoose: Search-focused content marketing.

Turn customer questions into useful articles.

✅ Content opportunity research.
✅ SEO topic planning.
✅ Articles with supporting images.
✅ Publishing support.

Let’s go back to that wholesale business.

Vlozy helps create a video about the frustration of managing orders through WhatsApp and spreadsheets.

Blogoose helps create an article answering:

“How can small wholesale businesses manage customer orders without spreadsheets?”

One helps people recognize a problem.

The other helps people research a better way to handle it.

Same product. Same customer problem. Two opportunities to get discovered.

Neither guarantees viral videos, rankings, or sales.

But both can help reduce repetitive content production work while keeping your marketing focused on real customer needs.

Because I believe founders should spend more time understanding their customers than manually producing every piece of marketing content.

That’s what I’m building Verthilix to help with.

If you’re running a SaaS, agency, or small business and spending hours every week creating content:

📩 DM me “GROWTH” + your website.

I’ll help identify the customer problems worth creating content around, which repetitive tasks could be automated, and whether Vlozy + Blogoose makes sense for your business.

🔎 Or search “Verthilix” on Google.

Your customers don’t just want to know what your software does.

They want to understand what becomes easier when they start using it.

Founders, when you demonstrate your product, do you start with its features or with the problem your customer experiences?

From the craftsman setting tile to the artist patching synth cables and the coach guiding neurodivergent minds, Michael Alexander Smith has lived his life across multiple creative avenues. Yet beneath every endeavor runs a single continuous thread: his journey with the Three Principles (3Ps) Understanding of Mind, Thought, and Consciousness, articulated by Sydney Banks.

The Foundations: Uncovering the Inside-Out Nature of Reality

Michael’s immersion in the 3Ps started with a pivotal insight into how human experience is constructed. Prior to discovering this paradigm, like many of us, it was easy to believe that external circumstances—demanding clients, physical wear and tear, or creative blocks—dictated internal peace.

Through the lens of Mind (the universal intelligence behind life), Thought (the creative power generating our moment-to-moment experience), and Consciousness (the awareness that makes it feel real), everything flipped. The realization that we live in the feeling of our thinking, not the feeling of our circumstances, laid the foundation for a profound shift in how Michael navigates both his working life and inner world.

Living the Principles Across Every Endeavor

The true test of any spiritual or psychological understanding is how it manifests when you’re on your knees fitting a floor or standing in front of a live crowd. For Michael, the 3Ps isn't a theory to hold onto; it's a living, practical awareness integrated seamlessly across his roles:

MAS Tiling (The Craftsman): Tiling demands precision, patience, and physical stamina. Understanding the fluid nature of thought allows Michael to drop the friction of overthinking, step into a state of flow on job sites across North Kent, and handle daily operational challenges without carrying unnecessary psychological weight home.

Mooky Musik & Astroscapes (The Creative): In the studio and during live sound experiments, the 3Ps light the way for unmasked creative expression. When you realize that creative blocks are simply transient thought-forms rather than personal defects, music becomes an effortless unfolding. From solo acoustic pieces to live hardware sets, the music flows directly from a quiet mind.

Michael A Smith ADHD Creative Coaching (The Guide): As a coach certified by the Association for Coaching, Michael uses the Inside-Out understanding to ground his work with neurodivergent artists and professionals. Rather than treating ADHD or creative intensity as something broken that needs fixing, he points clients back to their innate health, resilience, and quiet wisdom.
The Core Takeaway: Returning to Innate Wholeness
Over years of exploring this paradigm, the key insight remains disarmingly simple: wellbeing isn't something you construct; it’s what’s left when busy thinking settles.

Whether you know him as Michael the tiler, Mooky the musician, or Michael A Smith the coach, the underlying message is identical—you are already whole, your thoughts are temporary, and wisdom is always waiting in the quiet spaces between them.

For a deeper dive into the origin of this insight, watch this short animated introduction to Sydney Banks' core discovery:

Learn more about Sydney Banks and the Three Principles.

This video offers a concise, accessible overview of how Mind, Thought, and Consciousness shape our psychological reality from the inside out.

@WhiteHouse @PressSec 🥇👍🫡🇺🇸💞: Trump second-term scorecard — November 8, 2026

Coverage: substantive changes since the October 8 edition. Scores are analytical assessments of delivery against the administration’s stated agenda, not approval ratings: 0 = reversed/defeated; 5 = mixed or partial delivery; 10 = durably completed with demonstrated results.

The prior visual’s numeric scores are not available in the record, so I have not reconstructed or invented them. The arrows compare the verified policy position on October 8 with today; every current score was recalculated from current evidence.

New since the previous daily check

Confirmed fact — November 7: Trump publicly directed the Justice Department to investigate Democrats whom he accused of making criminal threats through planned congressional investigations and document demands. He offered no evidence of a crime, and DOJ had not announced an investigation or formal action as of this check. A prior DOJ effort to indict Senator Elissa Slotkin and other lawmakers was rejected by a grand jury. 

Analysis: This qualifies as a material institutional development because it is an explicit presidential instruction to examine political opponents and prospective congressional oversight. It is currently an announced directive, not an implemented prosecution, so it is reflected as heightened risk rather than a completed action.

Confirmed developments by category: Category

Verified change since October 8

Delivery status

Analytical score

Immigration

DHS’s October 14 final rule ended automatic extensions for certain expiring employment authorizations. The Fifth Circuit ruled 10–7 on October 23 that covered immigration detainees have no constitutional right to individualized bond hearings in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi; on October 27, the Supreme Court left in place the nationwide elimination of immigration judges’ “administrative closure” authority. Conversely, courts restored 21-day asylum-interview notice and rescheduling protections for unaccompanied children through November 13 and paused DHS’s new 10-day refugee-status termination deadline through December 4. 

Materially advanced, but partly blocked. Enforcement authority expanded through rules and court victories; two accelerated procedures are temporarily enjoined. No newer complete CBP/ICE outcome dataset was available, so no fresh removals or border-volume claim is included.

5.5/10 ↔

Taxation

No broad tax bill, major revenue measure or significant tax-rule implementation was enacted during the period. The October 20 Clergy Act made a narrow Social Security-coverage change for ministers, but it does not materially alter the administration’s overall tax record. 

No material change. Previously enacted tax legislation remains the principal achievement.

7.0/10 ↔

Economy

BEA’s October 29 advance estimate showed third-quarter real GDP growing at a 3.4% annual rate, versus 2.2% in Q2; private domestic final sales grew 4.9%. BLS reported 165,000 jobs added in October, 4.1% unemployment, manufacturing employment up 19,000 and wages up 3.1% year over year. However, involuntary part-time employment rose by 339,000. ISM’s October manufacturing index increased to 55.5, its tenth expansion month.  The October 22 housing order launched mortgage-insurance, title-review and manufactured-housing initiatives, but most benefits remain contingent on agency implementation. 

Measured improvement plus material policy advancement. Growth and hiring strengthened, but causation cannot be assigned solely to presidential policy and affordability remains weak.

6.5/10 ↑

Trade

The October 16 Graham Act implementation order formally specified 500% Russia tariffs and 100% secondary tariffs—but simultaneously waived the sanctions, restrictions and duties, leaving the headline rates inoperative.

text:
$VSH KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM VISHAY INTERTECHNOLOGY’S Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Vishay’s results indicate that the electronics recovery is broadening through industrial power, AI infrastructure, specialized passive components, and defense applications, rather than being confined to leading-edge semiconductors. The strongest evidence is the combination of 20% year-over-year volume growth, 26% distribution sell-through growth, a 1.29 book-to-bill ratio, and continued margin expansion despite input-cost inflation. The most actionable distinction is between suppliers monetizing higher component content and manufacturing utilization, and distributors financing the resulting inventory and receivables expansion. The former can generate substantial operating leverage; the latter can report exceptional earnings while consuming cash. The following read-throughs have high conviction in their economic direction, but their incremental trading significance varies because several affected companies had already reported comparable strength before Vishay’s call. Subsequent disclosures through November 6 are distinguished from information available on November 4.

PASSIVE COMPONENTS

SPECIALIZED POWER PASSIVES HAVE A CONTENT-GROWTH OPPORTUNITY, NOT MERELY A RESTOCKING CYCLE (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: Yageo Corporation (2327: Taiwan) and TDK Corporation (6762: Japan). Direction: positive. Magnitude: high for relevant power-capacitor, resistor, and magnetic-component businesses; potentially substantial for Yageo’s consolidated earnings and moderate for the more diversified TDK. Conviction: high on demand and operating leverage, but not on an indefinite scarcity-pricing premium.

The critical call evidence is that passive components represented 52% of Vishay’s revenue, alongside record resistor bookings and record demand for polymer capacitors associated with AI servers. Management explained that customers increasingly incorporate “multiple passive components within their same power architectures,” including current-sense resistors, power resistors, high-voltage capacitors, inductors, magnetics, and protection devices. Industrial revenue increased 43% year over year and 12% sequentially. This is stronger evidence than a generic AI-demand statement because it identifies both the applications and the component functions receiving incremental spending.

The transmission mechanism is increased content within power-conversion and distribution systems, combined with greater system deployment. Higher power density, tighter voltage tolerances, transient-load requirements, and efficiency constraints can increase demand for specialized capacitance, current sensing, filtering, and magnetics. For qualified suppliers, higher shipments improve utilization, while a more demanding product mix can improve revenue and gross profit per application. The opportunity is not simply more capacitors per server; it is a shift toward components whose electrical, thermal, reliability, and packaging requirements support greater value added.

Yageo provides particularly direct exposure through its tantalum capacitors, resistors, and broader passive portfolio. Reporting from its October 29 briefing indicated that AI applications approached 20% of Q3 revenue, compared with 16% in Q2, and that industrial revenue increased more than 40% year over year. It also described plans to expand tantalum-capacitor and MLCC capacity by 10% to 15% during 2027. Vishay therefore corroborates a demand pattern already visible at a major competitor, reducing the likelihood that the entire improvement is unique to Vishay’s share gains.

TDK’s own latest briefing provides complementary evidence. First-half passive-component sales increased 25.3% to approximately ¥358 billion, while segment operating profit increased to approximately ¥39.6 billion, or 2.7 times the prior-year level. Management specifically identified AI data-center demand for ceramic, aluminum-electrolytic, and film capacitors. This demonstrates that the opportunity is distributed across technologies rather than requiring polymer tantalum to displace MLCCs universally. TDK’s exposure is meaningful, but its battery and other businesses dilute the consolidated sensitivity.

The near-term catalysts are continued monthly sales strength at Yageo, subsequent quarterly margin delivery, and customer qualification updates. TDK’s November 10–13 electronica presentations can clarify product positioning, but demonstrations are not production awards. The longer-duration shift is rising specialized passive content across power architectures. The principal restraint is supply expansion: Vishay’s polymer capacity additions and Yageo’s planned expansion argue against capitalizing current tightness as a permanent condition. The strongest positive thesis is sustained shipment and mix improvement, not unlimited pricing power.

PRINTED CIRCUIT BOARDS AND DEFENSE ELECTRONICS

PCB AVAILABILITY IS BECOMING A MORE IMPORTANT PRODUCTION CONSTRAINT (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected company: TTM Technologies (TTMI: United States). Direction: positive. Magnitude: high at the consolidated level because data-center and networking applications represented 41% of TTM’s Q3 sales and aerospace and defense represented 34%. Conviction: high on demand relevance and the value of qualified capacity; a specific incremental pricing benefit cannot be quantified.

When asked about the risk of a missing critical component preventing completed-system shipments, Vishay identified “shortages of PCBs in some cases, more in AI,” with some instances in automotive. Management added that these shortages had not become a “showstopper.” This distinction is important: PCB availability is a demonstrated procurement concern, but the call does not establish widespread production stoppages or canceled demand.

The transmission mechanism favors manufacturers of qualified, technologically demanding boards over suppliers of readily substitutable commodity products. AI compute and high-speed networking require increasingly complex interconnects, demanding signal integrity, thermal performance, multilayer construction, and manufacturing consistency. Where a specific board is difficult to replace without qualification, available production capacity becomes more valuable. Higher demand can support utilization, favorable mix, and improved customer commitments, provided the supplier can manufacture the required technology at acceptable yields.

Vishay also reported significant telecommunications volume growth associated with 800-gigabit and 1.6-terabit network switches. That creates an additional demand channel for advanced PCBs beyond accelerator motherboards. Separately, aerospace and defense revenue increased 23% year over year, with Americas aerospace and defense book-to-bill reaching 1.64 as customers positioned orders against funded programs. These are distinct markets, but both favor reliable, qualified electronics production.

TTM’s October 22 release already reported a 2.13 consolidated book-to-bill ratio, $2.0 billion of aerospace and defense program backlog, and 115% reported year-over-year growth in data-center and networking revenue. Vishay’s subsequent commentary strengthens the interpretation that customer demand is encountering specialized supply constraints rather than merely reflecting speculative enthusiasm for future AI projects.

The near-term catalyst is TTM’s ability to convert its already disclosed order strength into shipments and maintain margins without excessive expediting, yield losses, or qualification delays. Since TTM reported before Vishay, this is corroboration of the forward outlook rather than a prediction of its completed Q3 results. The longer-duration benefit is the increasing technical and qualification burden of advanced boards, which can support customer retention and better returns on qualified capacity.

The limitation is that not all PCB capacity is interchangeable. Vishay did not identify TTM as the supplier involved in the reported shortages, and no specific incremental contract can be assigned. TTM’s acquisitions also affect its forward revenue perimeter, so reported growth should not automatically be interpreted as organic expansion. The high-conviction conclusion is that TTM’s core end-market and technology exposures align closely with the constraints identified on the call.

ELECTRONICS DISTRIBUTION

THE RECOVERY IS CONSUMPTION-SUPPORTED, WITH ADDITIONAL SALES POTENTIAL FROM TARGETED REPLENISHMENT (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected companies: Arrow Electronics (ARW: United States) and Avnet (AVT: United States). Direction: positive for component-distribution revenue and operating earnings. Magnitude: high for Avnet’s consolidated business and Arrow’s Global Components segment; somewhat lower for Arrow as a whole because enterprise computing has different demand drivers. Conviction: high on the operating-demand signal, without assuming that all Vishay share gains expand total distributor sales.

Vishay reported distribution revenue growth of 30% year over year and 9% sequentially, with distribution contributing 76% of its sequential revenue increase. More importantly, distributor POS increased 26% year over year and 5% sequentially while global inventory remained at 18 weeks. Management stated that distributors wanted additional inventory but were struggling to replenish because components were being consumed. This is materially stronger evidence than sell-in growth alone.

Arrow and Avnet participate directly in Vishay’s distribution network. The transmission mechanism is greater availability of saleable products, increased order fulfillment, and higher transaction volume across industrial, power, aerospace, and AI applications. Vishay’s addition of more than 17,000 distributor SKUs also expands the assortment available to serve customer bills of materials. Higher throughput can spread distribution infrastructure, engineering support, and administrative costs over a larger sales base.

However, the benefit is not equal to Vishay’s reported growth rate. Some Vishay sales may replace competing suppliers already carried by the same distributors. The 57% increase in units consumed through distribution is also distinct from the 26% POS growth figure and should not be treated as equivalent dollar growth. The positive industry conclusion rests on rising sell-through and persistent replenishment demand, not on transferring Vishay’s company-specific share gains directly into distributor forecasts.

Avnet’s November 4 release independently reported growth across all Electronic Components regions and Farnell. Excluding its extra fiscal week, company sales increased 71% year over year and 21% sequentially. Arrow’s November 5 release subsequently reported 43% growth in Global Components sales and described growing backlog and book-to-bill ratios well above parity. These disclosures confirm that Vishay’s strength is occurring within a broader channel recovery.

The geographic signal is particularly useful. Vishay distributor inventory stood at 12 weeks in Asia, 15 weeks in Europe, and 35 weeks in the Americas. Asia therefore appears to offer the clearest targeted replenishment opportunity, especially for individual parts with only 3 to 4 weeks of supply. The Americas figure argues against applying a universal restocking assumption across regions. These are Vishay-specific inventories, not direct measurements of Arrow’s or Avnet’s complete portfolios.

Near-term catalysts are December-quarter shipment conversion, supplier availability, and sustained POS growth. The longer-duration benefit is the value of broad product availability and technical support when customers need multiple technologies and dependable fulfillment. The operating signal is positive, but the cash consequences are substantially less favorable.

REPLENISHMENT TRANSFERS A LARGE FUNDING BURDEN INTO THE CHANNEL (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected companies: Avnet (AVT: United States) and Arrow Electronics (ARW: United States). Direction: negative for near-term free cash flow and capital-return flexibility, despite positive revenue and earnings momentum. Magnitude: high at the consolidated cash-flow level for both companies. Conviction: high; current financial disclosures already demonstrate the mechanism.

The supporting Vishay commentary is explicit: distributors want to put more product on shelves, pull in backlog, and extend ordering coverage. Vishay is also passing through input-cost increases. The less favorable consequence is that distributors must finance more inventory and receivables, often at higher replacement costs, before collecting from customers. Strong demand can therefore improve reported earnings while increasing cash requirements.

Stable inventory weeks do not imply stable inventory dollars. When sales and cost throughput rise, maintaining the same weeks of coverage requires more absolute inventory. A distributor can simultaneously improve inventory efficiency and consume significant cash. This is particularly consequential in a low-margin business, where the working capital needed to support incremental revenue can be large relative to the associated profit.

Avnet’s November 4 financial statements illustrate the point. Inventory increased from approximately $6.07 billion to $8.18 billion, while quarterly operating cash flow was negative $842.4 million. Inventory and receivables together absorbed approximately $3.02 billion before approximately $1.81 billion of supplier financing through accounts payable. These are company-wide figures, not amounts attributable specifically to Vishay. They nevertheless demonstrate the funding intensity of the same expansion pattern described on Vishay’s call.

Arrow’s subsequently released November 5 statements reported negative $441.4 million of quarterly operating cash flow and approximately $1.38 billion of inventory-related cash absorption. Arrow’s enterprise-computing activities also affect receivable and payable settlement patterns, so its total funding requirement cannot be assigned solely to component replenishment. The consolidated cash burden is nevertheless clear.

The negative read-through is not a liquidity-crisis thesis. Avnet reported return on working capital improving to 25% from 19% sequentially, and guided to similar sequential interest expense. Higher working-capital investment may therefore be economically attractive even while reducing current cash available for buybacks or debt reduction. The appropriate distinction is between profitable growth and immediately distributable cash.

The near-term catalysts are subsequent cash-flow conversion, inventory-dollar growth, funding requirements, and capital-return decisions. The longer-duration risk emerges if customer order horizons shorten after distributors have replenished at elevated costs. That would expose the channel to slower turns and inventory adjustments. Such a reversal has not been established, but the current funding burden is already material. Across a portfolio, long positions in component manufacturers and distributors share demand exposure while having very different cash-flow timing.

POWER SEMICONDUCTORS

INDUSTRIAL AND AI POWER SUPPORT MARGIN RECOVERY, BUT AUTOMOTIVE UNIT GROWTH IS NOT THE DRIVER (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected company: onsemi (ON: United States). Direction: positive for industrial and AI power revenue and manufacturing utilization; restrictive for expectations of a broad automotive-volume rebound. Magnitude: moderate positive at the consolidated level, with greater sensitivity in the relevant power-product businesses. Conviction: high on the end-market divergence, without assigning Vishay’s margins or growth rates to onsemi.

Vishay reported industrial revenue growth of 43% year over year, strong design activity across MOSFETs, diodes, protection devices, and passives, and semiconductor book-to-bill of 1.28. Management also increased Korean foundry loading to support AI customer deliveries in Q4, with further increases planned into the first half of 2027. These statements indicate current production requirements, not merely distant design opportunities.

The transmission mechanism for onsemi is greater demand for qualified power-conversion, switching, and protection products, followed by improved utilization and fixed-cost absorption. The benefit depends on product architecture and customer qualification rather than simply the number of AI servers. Industrial power infrastructure and energy-management systems provide additional demand beyond the compute board itself.

Onsemi’s November 2 release already reported AI data-center revenue growth of 39% sequentially and 175% year over year. Its non-GAAP gross margin increased 190 basis points sequentially to 41.2%, with Q4 guidance of 41.5% to 43.5%. Vishay’s subsequent commentary provides external confirmation that the power-demand environment supporting that progression is broader than onsemi-specific design wins.

The automotive distinction prevents overextension of the bullish interpretation. Vishay’s automotive revenue increased 7% year over year, but management said that vehicle production was generally flat and expected approximately flat automotive revenue in Q4. Growth was attributed to electronic content and new programs rather than a substantial increase in vehicle units. The implication for onsemi is that industrial and AI power can support recovery without requiring a strong automotive production rebound. Automotive exposure alone is not sufficient grounds to extrapolate Vishay’s industrial growth.

Vishay’s assertions of share gains also create a competitive qualification. Industry growth does not mean every power-semiconductor supplier gains share, and Vishay did not identify the competitors losing business. No specific displacement of onsemi is established. Conversely, Vishay’s capital-spending burden should not be transferred to onsemi: onsemi reported $489 million of Q3 free cash flow, demonstrating a materially different current cash-conversion profile.

The near-term catalysts are delivery against onsemi’s already issued Q4 margin and revenue outlook and evidence that AI growth remains incremental rather than merely offsetting weaker applications. The longer-duration shift is greater power-management content across data centers, industrial systems, and energy infrastructure. This is a selective power-semiconductor positive, not an indiscriminate signal to increase exposure to all automotive or commodity discrete suppliers.

ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT AND GRID INFRASTRUCTURE

COMPONENT CONSUMPTION VALIDATES ACTIVE POWER-INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDOUT, NOT JUST PROJECT ANNOUNCEMENTS (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: Eaton Corporation plc (ETN: Ireland). Direction: positive. Magnitude: high strategic relevance and moderate incremental earnings significance from this call alone, because Eaton’s electrical businesses already represent approximately 78% of quarterly sales and have disclosed strong demand independently. Conviction: high on end-market confirmation; no specific Canadian project award is established.

Vishay identified new Americas projects in power management, smart grids, and industrial automation moving into mass production. It also reported winning an additional smart-grid infrastructure program connected with Canadian data-center construction and EV adoption. Demand remained strong for high-voltage DC and data-center power supplies, while customers expanded the range of components incorporated into power architectures.

The transmission mechanism is increased deployment of electrical distribution, conversion, protection, and control equipment as power-intensive infrastructure moves from planning into manufacturing and installation. Component consumption is useful evidence because it indicates activity within the physical production chain. It does not prove that every announced data-center project will be energized on schedule, but it is more concrete than an increase in announced project capacity alone.

Eaton’s product exposure aligns with these applications through its electrical distribution and power-management businesses. Its November 3 release reported 22% organic growth in Electrical Americas and 27% organic growth in Electrical Global, with a rolling electrical book-to-bill ratio of 1.2. Vishay therefore corroborates the breadth of demand already visible in Eaton’s results. It does not establish an additional order award or justify adding Vishay’s growth rate to Eaton’s existing outlook.

The particularly important implication is that data centers and grid reinforcement are connected rather than independent investment themes. Additional computing load can require upstream utility upgrades, site-level electrical distribution, power conversion, and protection. Exposure to Eaton, specialized passive suppliers, power-semiconductor companies, and advanced PCB manufacturers can therefore represent repeated participation in the same capital-spending chain, even when portfolio classifications suggest diversification.

The near-term catalyst is conversion of existing electrical backlog into shipments and cash while maintaining execution through capacity expansion. Eaton’s Q3 free cash flow of approximately $1.03 billion provides a favorable contrast with the cash consumption reported by electronics distributors. The longer-duration benefit is the need to expand and modernize electrical infrastructure alongside power-intensive computing and broader electrification.

The principal limitation is geographic and contractual. Vishay did not identify the Canadian project owner, equipment integrator, or utility. Assigning the project to Eaton, or to a specific Canadian utility, would be unsupported. The high-conviction conclusion is that current component demand validates the broader electrical-infrastructure spending cycle, while project-specific revenue and timing remain unallocated.

SOURCE BASIS

The principal source is Vishay’s November 4, 2026 earnings call and accompanying financial disclosures. Peer verification uses TTM’s October 22 results, reporting from Yageo’s October 29 briefing, TDK’s latest first-half briefing and October 20 product announcement, onsemi’s November 2 results, Eaton’s November 3 results, Avnet’s November 4 results, and Arrow’s November 5 results. Directional assessments describe business and earnings implications, not assured share-price reactions or evidence that the information is unpriced.

text:
UGANDA CONFRONTS ITS FUTURE: THE CONSOCIATIONAL DEMOCRACY AGREEMENT PROPOSAL BY GEN. SALIM SALEH AND PROF. OGENGA OTUNNU.

By Keefa Nuwahereza.

A working paper circulating in Ugandan political circles has shifted national debate away from the narrow question of who will succeed President Yoweri Museveni after more than four decades in power. Authored by Gen. Caleb Akandwanaho (widely known as Salim Saleh) and historian Prof. Ogenga Otunnu, the document titled *Consociational Democracy Agreement: Addressing the Root Causes and Consequences of Sectarianism, Exclusion, Marginalisation and Conflicts in Uganda* proposes a structured five-year framework from 2026 to 2031. It argues that lasting stability requires a public, inclusive settlement addressing deep-rooted grievances rather than another private bargain among elites.

The paper does not nominate a successor. Instead, it asks what political settlement can survive the exit of a leader who has governed since 1986 without simply recreating the cycles of exclusion that have characterised successive Ugandan regimes. Saleh, Museveni’s younger brother, a bush-war veteran who commanded forces during the 1986 capture of Kampala, former army commander, and current Chief Coordinator of Operation Wealth Creation, brings insider weight that makes the proposal difficult for the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) to ignore. Prof. Otunnu, a DePaul University historian with expertise in African history, forced migration, and conflict, has served as an adviser to Saleh and previously contributed to analyses of northern Uganda’s conflicts.

Historical roots of division.

The paper’s central historical claim is that Uganda’s religious, ethnic, and regional cleavages were not ancient or inevitable. They were invented, politicised, and repeatedly weaponised. It traces influences from the 19th-century arrival of Islam at the Buganda court of Kabaka Suna, followed by Protestant and Catholic missionaries in the 1870s, through British colonial indirect rule that hardened identities, and into every post-independence government. The 1962 UPC-Kabaka Yekka alliance offered temporary accommodation for Buganda but excluded significant groups, notably Catholics aligned with the Democratic Party. The 1979 Moshi Conference after Idi Amin’s fall sought broader inclusion yet failed to resolve underlying issues. NRM-era cooperation arrangements with parties such as the Democratic Party and Uganda People’s Congress delivered periods of relative calm but were negotiated privately. Ordinary party members and communities were left as permanent “outsiders,” unable to scrutinise terms or enforce delivery. Sectarian identities hardened rather than diminished, while concrete grievances over land, regional inequality, education access, youth unemployment, and public services remained unaddressed.

This analysis draws on a long record of elite bargains that produced temporary stability without transforming the distribution of opportunity or accountability. The authors warn that such patterns freeze identities instead of reducing their political salience.

The proposed Consociational Democracy Agreement.

Against this record, the paper advances a Consociational Democracy Agreement for 2026–2031. Consociational democracy, in the classic sense associated with political scientists such as Arend Lijphart, involves power-sharing and consensus-seeking among competing groups rather than pure majority rule in deeply divided societies. Examples cited in related discussions include arrangements in Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Lebanon, and Northern Ireland. The Ugandan proposal does not seek permanent ethnic or religious quotas that would institutionalise divisions. Its explicit aim is to reduce the political weight of sectarian identity while tackling material grievances that drive people toward identity-based protection.

A non-negotiable requirement is that any agreement must be a written, publicly gazetted document available in local languages. Private understandings among party leaders are rejected as insufficient for democratic legitimacy, transparency, or the social contract between leaders and citizens. The paper criticises past NRM-DP and NRM-UPC deals on precisely these grounds: they may have aided cohesion but lacked the knowledge or consent of the communities they claimed to represent, producing temporary calm without durable inclusion.

Structure: the National Consociational Council.

Implementation would centre on a National Consociational Council with three chambers. The Elite Cooperation Chamber would handle political-level negotiations among government and political parties. The Grassroots and Multi-Stakeholder Chamber (sometimes called the People’s Chamber) would bring in civil society, religious and cultural leaders, women, youth, labour, and other groups to ensure community concerns shape agreements. The Technical and Implementation Secretariat (or Delivery Secretariat) would translate commitments into funded government programmes, budgets, timelines, and measurable targets. Religious and cultural leaders, civil society, women, youth, and labour would hold structural rather than ceremonial roles.

The process is envisioned in stages: identify grievances, conduct joint elite and grassroots dialogue, reach and publish formal agreements, implement concrete redress measures, monitor progress independently with public reporting, and return unresolved issues to further dialogue. Government ministries would incorporate relevant commitments into policies and budgets. The framework is presented as complementary to existing institutions such as Parliament and Cabinet, not a replacement. It is described as a long-term programme, not a short-term project, requiring sustained involvement over five years.

Key grievances targeted.

Land disputes feature prominently, with mediation examples already tested, such as Saleh directing Otunnu to address a conflict in Pader that threatened a cassava starch factory. Regional economic inequality, youth unemployment, commercialisation of education that reinforces rather than reduces gaps, inadequate public investment in schools, corruption, and weaknesses in service delivery are identified as fault lines. The paper notes that education has often failed as an equaliser because of household income differences, geographical disparities, and other structural factors. Electoral credibility, institutional independence, and limits on money’s influence in politics are treated as essential foundations. Regional voting patterns are acknowledged as politically significant even where national results have favoured the incumbent across most areas between 2006 and 2026, with exceptions in northern Uganda earlier and central Uganda more recently.

Political context and presentation.

The proposal was first shared with newly elected NRM MPs at a Kyankwanzi retreat in April 2026, later presented to the NRM Caucus, discussed at a political parties’ retreat in Jinja in mid-October 2026 organised with support from the Netherlands Institute for Multiparty Democracy, and taken to President Museveni, religious leaders, and opposition parties. Saleh has urged parliamentary committee chairpersons to study it, citing Museveni’s past record of compromises with political actors and former insurgents. He has spoken of sparing the 35–55 generation from “inheriting our generational quarrels” and of seeking progress within three to six months toward “the Uganda we want.” He has also engaged on the situation of detained opposition leader Dr Kizza Besigye, including arranging improved medical care after finding him in poor health, following a public signal from Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba.

Reports indicate discussions within the ruling establishment about succession, including Muhoozi’s publicly expressed ambitions for 2031. Saleh’s public profile on the proposal has raised questions about internal dynamics, though sources do not establish that he is positioning himself as an alternative candidate. The timing, early in Museveni’s latest term and amid open talk of 2031, means the document is not read solely as abstract theory. Saleh’s networks across the military, party, and economic programmes give the initiative practical weight inside the system that has long treated succession as largely non-negotiable.

Reactions and scepticism.

The proposal has drawn both interest and sharp questions. Supporters see potential for structured inclusion that past elite deals lacked. Critics, including some opposition figures, ask whether an establishment that has governed for forty years can credibly lead its own reform. A senior National Unity Platform official has expressed support for genuine dialogue in principle while remaining wary of co-optation, citing the example of Democratic Party leader Norbert Mao’s cooperation arrangement. Ibrahim Ssemujju Nganda of the People’s Front for Freedom has voiced scepticism from exile. An open letter from Dr Joseph Tindyebwa challenged the authors on forty years of NRM rule, unresolved national questions, and the need for sincerity. Mulengera News coverage highlighted how the paper’s critique of private deals reopened tensions within the Democratic Party over the NRM-DP arrangement.

Observer commentary notes the risk that dialogue could substitute for accountability or that the Council could become another parallel structure absorbed into patronage networks. The paper’s own historical critique of previous NRM-era accommodations makes such doubts more pointed. Whether structures acquire real teeth—measurable changes in land mediation, education resource distribution, youth employment funding, and community monitoring—will determine outcomes. Uganda has never had a peaceful presidential handover since independence. The document does not guarantee one. It does make it harder to treat the post-Museveni question as purely internal to family or party, and harder for opposition to dismiss every overture as automatically illegitimate.

Broader implications.

The initiative sits alongside other dialogue tracks, including IPOD and reported Besigye-related talks. It emphasises that NRM rule from 1986 has represented the most sustained effort against sectarianism, yet the costs of incomplete integration have included lives and property. Implementation would require legal and constitutional adjustments in some areas, according to comments attributed to Justice Minister Mao. Practical tests already include community-level interventions. Challenges remain in moving from policy discussions to sustained grassroots engagement and in securing buy-in across a polarised landscape where many opposition supporters interpret dialogue as potential surrender.

If successful, the framework could redefine the rules any future leader must meet by linking elite negotiations to community concerns and budgets. If it remains a high-level document quietly absorbed, it will confirm readings of managed transition. The authors stress that the goal is not to wish away cleavages or eliminate them administratively—approaches tried before, from banning Kabaka Yekka to proscribing certain religious politics—but to confront their roots through inclusive, public, monitored processes.

As of early November 2026, the working paper (described variously as 128 or 137 pages) continues to circulate in consultations rather than as a fully open download. Media summaries from outlets including The Observer, Nile Post, Watchdog Uganda, ChimpReports, and Mulengera News have driven public discussion. The conversation has moved, at least temporarily, from inheritance of the seat to the conditions any inheritor will face. Whether this produces a more durable settlement or a more elaborate form of continuity remains the open question facing Uganda’s political actors, communities, and institutions.

Hey Tibo, I have several ideas on how to improve Astra and how OpenAI can win the “AI wars.”

Most importantly, I highly recommend focusing on profit from creating new IP WITH the AI.

Find a cure for a disease and patent it.

Develop a new material that’s better than anything on the market.

Create a new type of oil that increases engine life.

Build a pipeline:

Your users and engineers improve the AI → The AI is used to research scientific bottlenecks with high commercial potential → Patent the resulting inventions under OpenAI → License those patents → Repeat.

Do that enough, and OpenAI could become very profitable. I think you could start seeing results within a year.

To support that pipeline, create competitions that concentrate your user base on developing cutting-edge solutions to improve the product.

Yes, you have highly paid engineers and great talent, but you also have an immense talent pool of users, each equipped with cutting-edge AI: your latest frontier model.

Offer prizes: $5,000 USD to improve X or Y. Set up an effective team dedicated to reviewing submissions.

MAKE THE PUBLIC YOUR OWN R&D ARMY.

Use that to maintain a lead over Anthropic and the other frontier companies. Spread the wealth early. For the annual compensation of one frontier engineer, say, $500,000 USD, you could potentially generate enough improvements to Astra to justify ten times that investment, if not more.

That’s why I think OpenAI should play the long game. Don’t play for what AI is today or how it’s used today. Play for where it’ll be in five years. Then ten. And so on.

You shouldn’t even prioritize profiting directly from your users. Build a reputation for generosity and smart pricing, like you did with the resets. Absolutely avoid things you KNOW will piss people off.

You’ll face constant pressure to turn a profit. This is a corporation, and there’s pressure to maximize profits for shareholders.

Resist letting that dictate the strategy. That doesn’t play the long game. It lets an outside factor limit what you can do strategically. Take a risk. Be bold.

Look at Google. See how too much caution can leave you behind? This technology has immense potential for wealth creation.

On pricing, create a powerful funnel toward higher tiers by offering exclusive features that genuinely enhance the product, like you did with Ultrafast.

Release a $1,000 plan with unique productivity enhancements and first access to beta features. Give the higher tiers exclusive perks.

If users integrate AI into their lives (and I believe that will become increasingly common until “power user” describes the default population), you’ll have a very powerful funnel toward those higher tiers.

People will prioritize their subscriptions enough to earn the money to maintain them if the product becomes sufficiently profitable for them and vital to their work-life balance.

For the usage structure specifically, I’d suggest:

| Plan / price | Usage |
|--------------|-------|
| Plus: $20    | 1×    |
| Pro: $50     | 5×    |
| Pro: $100    | 12×   |
| Pro: $200    | 25×   |
| $500 tier    | 75×   |

The higher tiers should offer disproportionately more usage to incentivize upgrades. The psychology shouldn’t be “I’m getting double for paying double.” It should be “I’m saving money by spending more.”

Maintain those rates. Never lower quotas. Never raise prices. Stay the course for a year, then increasingly differentiate the tiers through genuinely valuable exclusive features. I believe that combination would put serious pressure on the competition.
