text:
My first severe burnout hit me back in 2018. It was not just routine fatigue, but a fundamental disillusionment with the market.

It started with conversations with peers, owners of marketing agencies in my home million-plus city. I looked inside their operations and was appalled. About 80 to 90% of it was outright theater: inflated rankings, fake traffic, painted reports. Nobody was even trying to deliver actual business results. People were just cynically monetizing the client's lack of competence.

It got under my skin so much that I decided to run an experiment and test this model myself. I took on a client and basically fed him lines for a year, manufacturing the illusion of progress. I stacked every dollar he paid me into a separate pile. I was convinced that after a couple of months he would snap out of it and say: "Man, this is pure garbage," and I would silently hand back every single cent.

A year passed. He never snapped out of it.

When I got tired of playing along with the circus, I told him I was terminating the contract. In response, he called repeatedly, practically begging me to keep going. The man was asking me to keep taking his money for doing absolutely nothing.

That broke me completely. I realized an ugly truth: this unethical imitation model works flawlessly. In regional small business, it covers 90% of the market. The client does not want to dig into the mechanics; he wants to buy a comfortable price point. The agency sells him that price along with a cheap illusion of control. Everyone is happy, and margins are great.

Your problems start the exact moment you genuinely want to deliver growth for the client's business.

To drive real growth, you have to dig into operations, overhaul processes, build end-to-end analytics, and pour in hundreds of hours that a small business simply cannot afford. I tested every model: pay-per-lead, revenue share, retainers tied to KPIs. In nine out of ten cases, you crash head-on into the core bottleneck of small business: the owner himself. Sales reps drop leads, the product lags behind, but the marketer who brought the wrong crowd always gets the blame.

When you decide to do the job properly, your addressable market shrinks to a razor-thin layer of mature companies. Meanwhile, the remaining 90% of the market has a massive, persistent appetite for fake marketing, with zero appetite for real change.

In 2018 and 2019, that realization knocked me out of the game for nearly a year. Total apathy and a complete dead end.

There is only one way out of this trap: stop selling cheap parlor tricks and bargain-bin leads to people who just need a sedative. Either you agree to be a low-budget clown, or you step into a completely different league. Move where people track unit economics instead of clicks, and where marketing is baked into the business model rather than slapped on like a patch on a leaky bucket.

text:
Tweet 9
The lock your carrier must give you free:

7 lines. A number you rent rather than own. 320 complaints in three years, then 1,611 in one. A regulator writing down that your address and your last bill don’t prove who you are. A 1980s protocol with no authentication running 800 networks. German bank accounts emptied in January 2017. And a free lock that is off by default.

Now the honest part.

The overwhelming majority of SIM changes are legitimate, and the FCC says so in the order itself. Carriers process these constantly for people who genuinely lost a phone. Any authentication strong enough to stop every attacker also strands real customers at the worst moment of their week — and that tradeoff is why the old process was weak, not pure negligence.

SS7 attacks are also not cheap or common. They require access to a telecom network, which means either buying it from a complicit small operator or being a state. The Register’s 2017 reporting noted carriers’ position that exploitation demands significant technical and financial resources. For most people, SIM swapping is the realistic threat and SS7 is not.

And the FBI’s figures are complaints, not measurements. Rising numbers partly reflect rising awareness and reporting. The 15-fold jump I calculated in Line 2 is real arithmetic on real published figures — and some of it is people finally knowing what to call this.

“You can change a password. You cannot change who your carrier gives your number to.”

“SMS is not your second factor. It’s your only one.”

Next time a service offers you two-factor by text, don’t accept the default. Ask whether the same channel is also the account recovery route — because if it is, the second factor is decorative.

And the two minutes worth spending right now. Open your carrier’s app and find the setting called Number Lock, SIM Protection, Port Freeze or similar. Switch it on. The FCC required your carrier to offer it free in 2023, and it is almost certainly off.

Why keep this one. Not the lock. The FCC’s list of what doesn’t count as identity. Your birthday, your address, your last payment, your recent calls — a regulator formally ruled all of it insufficient. Every organisation still asking you those questions to verify you is using a method their own government has written off.

A person may attain wealth, status, power, or titles, yet the true essence of reality—the genuine standard of character, along with the sweetness and purity of truth—remains beyond their reach. Such individuals—dishonest, corrupt, and tainted—are shameless, reckless, and of the basest nature. They represent the worst of their kind; even if they happen to speak the truth, they may still be dishonest, corrupt, thieving, violent, or even murderous—a shameless group that enriches itself at the expense of the rights of the poor. To profane the sacred essence of creation—the fragrance of the heart—and to reduce women to mere objects for public display is an act of the utmost atrocity and contempt; it is a supreme insult to all of humanity. Wealth, status, or one’s occupation are not the root of our problems. An honest person can never be truly poor, for worldly wealth, power, titles, or fame do not define the state of the soul. In fact, these are often dangerous traps—a strategy designed to cultivate a class of dishonest people. The soul is neither inherently rich nor poor; and work is, at its core, a path illuminated by the light of the soul. Therefore, let us seek our true identity and wisdom at the source of truth. O soul, look back toward the distant past and contemplate the light of the future—toward a world that existed long before the 8.3 billion people who now inhabit this universe; yet, today, we all live in the presence of that very light.  Therefore, remain steadfast on the path of truth and build upon that foundation as much as you possibly can. For you are a living soul, and as such, you deserve our deepest respect. O soul, you are truly wonderful. You have come with the destiny of becoming the pure, fragrant heart of all creation—emerging as a brilliant, blue-green light, the very essence of life. Never abandon the truth, for you were born upon the path of truth; to forsake the truth is to sever your connection to the source of all existence in this universe. Thank you. By the will of God Almighty and the blessings of the Most Holy Virgin Mary, Princess Leonor de Todos los Santos de Borbón y Ortiz has emerged—a soul illuminated by a profound, blue-green cosmic aura, standing in the presence of the eternal and indestructible sun. I offer her my unwavering support and respect, for she is a sovereign reflection of that sacred Being who permeates all of creation. O soul, you are truly beautiful; you shall return, manifesting once more as this vibrant, blue-green light of life. You are ever in my thoughts, held with the deepest respect. The Supreme Being resides within her. Amen. This act of respect strengthens the foundation of truth. Thank you. To exploit women by depicting them in a state of nudity is an atrocious crime—a deep stain in the eyes of the entire universe. Therefore, as men, protect women and show them the utmost respect. To deprive women of their dignity is to plunge humanity into a darkness riddled with hatred, jealousy, aggression, violence, religious exploitation, and a craving for wealth and status—a truly humiliating existence. Life itself is neither a problem nor merely a human construct. Remain ever steadfast on the path of truth, for therein resides the Supreme Being. Amen.

🇱🇺 🇧🇪 Grand Duke Henri attended the inauguration of Drottning Astrids Församling of the Church of Sweden in Brussels. 

The ceremony was part of the celebrations marking the Centenary of the Marriage of Queen Astrid (née Princess of Sweden) & the future King Leopold III, as well as the 400th Anniversary of the Church of Sweden abroad.

As Grandson of Queen Astrid, Grand Duke Henri took part in the tribute alongside his first cousin, Princess Astrid of the Belgians. 

On the occasion, Their Royal Highnesses unveiled a new portrait of Queen Astrid & a commemorative brass plaque.

🇮🇳🪔 Deepawali with India’s Bravehearts! Rajnath Singh Celebrates Festival with Troops Along the Border in Sikkim

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh celebrated Deepawali on November 8, 2026, with soldiers of the Trishakti Corps (33 Corps) deployed in the forward areas of Sikkim, at Sherathang. He was accompanied by Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth and senior Army commanders.

Interacting with the troops, Rajnath Singh praised their courage, professionalism, high morale and unwavering commitment to guarding India’s borders in challenging high-altitude conditions. He described the soldiers as the brightest lights of Diwali, acknowledging their sacrifices and dedication while serving far away from their families.

The Defence Minister also urged soldiers to uphold discipline, courage and restraint, and continue strengthening the bond of trust and goodwill between the Indian Army and local communities.

During the visit, he paid tribute to fallen soldiers at the Sherathang War Memorial and offered prayers at the Baba Harbhajan Singh Memorial. He highlighted how war memorials preserve the legacy of bravehearts and inspire future generations with their courage and sacrifice.

Remembering the spirit of national unity, Rajnath Singh noted that soldiers from different states and communities had made the supreme sacrifice to protect the nation and its people.

Saluting the brave soldiers who stand guard so that India can celebrate Diwali in peace and security. 🇮🇳🙏

text:
🦆 The geese saved Rome in 390 BC. But a flock of wild ducks saved my grandfather in the 1950s

Throughout history, survival often comes down to bizarre, unpredictable variables.

In the 1950s, mandatory military service in Bulgaria lasted a grueling three years. If you were unlucky, you got assigned to the most remote, harsh borderlands, places like the cold hills of Ivaylovgrad. Poor infrastructure, severe weather, and the constant threat of border incidents made it a brutal posting for a young conscript, completely cut off from home.

That was precisely where my grandfather was sent.

🥚 The Unconventional Flock

Back at his family's small farm near Plovdiv, his parents were desperate for a way to get him transferred closer to home.

Years prior, they had done something completely impractical for regular farmers: they rescued an injured wild duck and a clutch of abandoned eggs from the nearby river reeds. They placed the eggs under a domestic hen, who raised the hatchlings as her own.

While most villagers raised standard livestock for meat and eggs, my great-grandparents kept this peculiar flock of healthy, beautiful, remarkably docile wild ducks simply out of care. It made zero economic sense at the time, until fate showed up on a motorcycle.

🏍️ The Trade of a Lifetime

A high-ranking military commander rode into the village searching for authentic decoy ducks for hunting. Word spread, and he was directed to the farm.

The moment he saw the birds, he was struck by their striking plumage and calm demeanor. He immediately offered to buy them on the spot.

My great-grandparents didn't ask for money. They asked for a favor: "Move our son to a safer posting closer to home."

The commander made a single phone call.

🎯 From Border Patrol to Officer's Quarters

Overnight, my grandfather was transferred from the harsh, high-risk border duty in Ivaylovgrad to a small, quiet officer barracks right in the heart of Plovdiv.

His new "hardship duty"? Maintaining the grounds, playing cards, and spending his days at the range practicing marksmanship with double-barreled shotguns and sniper rifles. He earned the official military specialty of "Shooter" while getting regular weekend leaves to visit the farm.

A generation later, my father didn't have the luxury of a duck trade, so his service wasn't nearly as easy. But by then, times had softened slightly, and he was fortunate enough to serve at an airfield near the city.

By the time my generation came around, mandatory conscription was abolished entirely in favor of a professional army. I never had to rely on a flock of ducks to alter a military posting, but to this day, "lucky duck" moments show up in my life as bizarre, statistical coincidences. 🦆

Random acts of care have a strange way of compounding over time. You never know which unconventional decision today will end up saving your family tomorrow.

Mr Zaidi, nobody forced anyone to join the army. I wrote about what a major earns, what comes out of his salary and what the job demands. Choosing to serve doesn’t make any of that irrelevant.

On tolls, an officer pays when travelling in a private car. The NHA exemption applies to armed forces vehicles with broad-arrow number plates. How does that become a personal perk for the officer?

As for CSD, take the same brand and size of milk carton in Rawalpindi and check the price at CSD, Imtiaz and Punjab Cash & Carry. It costs about the same at all three. Where’s the saving on that purchase?

What CSD offers through hire purchase is the option to pay in instalments. You can buy a fridge, a motorcycle or a car without paying the whole amount upfront. You still pay the full price, and once you add up the payments, it costs more than buying the same item in cash. You get more time to pay. Where’s the subsidy you’re counting?
